questions.question: ायदशनानुसारे दु:खस्य कारणं िकम् ?What is the cause of suffering according to the Nyāya system? a). धनं b). अहारं c). अानं d). अत्याग्रहं
questions.solution_html: अज्ञानं

questions.question: ----तु तृतीयकं |के न ?----tu trutiyakam.by which? / a). ऊजन b). तोयेन c). वायुना d). अेन
questions.solution_html: तोयेन

questions.question: िशवेन अिभिहतािन कित आसनािन सन्त ? / a). दश b). चतुरशीित लािण c). िवंशित d). ित्रंशत्
questions.solution_html: चतुरशीतत लक्षाति

questions.question: बादरायणेन रिचतं ग्रः कः ? Which is the text written by Badarayana? / a). वैशेिषकसूत्रम् b). योगसूत्रम् c). ायसूत्रम् d). वेदन्तसूत्रम्
questions.solution_html: वेदान्तसूत्रम्

questions.question: पीठशलभं वदन्त के ? / a). मुिनन्द्राः b). पुरुषाः c). योिगपुङ्गवैः d). देवाः
questions.solution_html: मुनीन्द्राः

questions.question: शीृ त्यपीत्वा क्रमेण नासानालैिववजयेत् -। / a). वातक्रम कपालभाित b). शीतक्रमेण कपालभाित c). ुत्क्रम कपालभाित d). कपालभाित
questions.solution_html: शीतक्रमेि कपालभातत

questions.question: लौिलकी नाम िकम् ? What is Louliki? / a). श्वसन शु b). पवनमागस्य शोधना c). कु ां पेशीचालनं d). नयनानां शु
questions.solution_html: श्वसन शुति

questions.question: िकम् समासाद्य प्राणायामं समस्यसेत् । / a). ानम् b). धारणम् c). नाडीशु d). मुा
questions.solution_html: नाडीशुति

questions.question: 'इडा ' अथात् | Meaning of 'Ida'-- / a). राहु b). सूयनाडी c). के तु d). चन्द्रनाडी
questions.solution_html: चन्द्रनाडी

questions.question: िचिक्रका नाम िकम् ? / a). ानं b). धारणा c). समािध d). आसनं
questions.solution_html: आसनं

questions.question: भारतीय तत्वानं प्रित लखु िटप्पणी िलखत | Write a short note on Indian philosophy.
questions.solution_html:
• Indian philosophy consists of philosophical traditions of the Indian
  • subcontinent. The philosophies are often called darśana, meaning "to see" or
  • "looking at.There are six major (āstika) schools of Vedic philosophy—Nyaya
  • Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mīmāṃsā and Vedanta—and three major non-Vedic
  • or heterodox (nāstika or sramanic) schools—Jain, Buddha and Charvaka.
questions.final_answer: or heterodox (nāstika or sramanic) schools—Jain, Buddha and Charvaka

questions.question: समग्रारों योगश्च । Holistic health and Yoga
questions.solution_html:
• Holistic yoga is a wellness practice that unites the mind, body, and spirit. It
  • goes beyond just physical exercise to include breathing, meditation, and
  • mindfulness. It helps lower stress, improves flexibility, and brings inner peace to
  • your daily life.

questions.question: िकम् नाम प्रत्याहारम् ?
questions.solution_html:
• Pratyahara: Withdrawal of the senses from external distractions.
  • स्वतवषयासम्प्रयोगे तचत्तस्वरूपानुकार इवेतन्द्रयािं प्रत्याहारः ।
questions.final_answer: Pratyahara: Withdrawal of the senses from external distractions

questions.question: िकम् नाम नौकासनम् ?
questions.solution_html:
• Naukasana (Boat Pose) is a core-strengthening yoga posture where your body
  • forms a "V" shape, balancing solely on your sit bones. It heavily engages the
  • abdominals, hip flexors, and spine. Regular practice is excellent for toning the
  • belly, aiding digestion, and improving balance.
  • उत्तानौ पादौ कृ त्वा हस्तौ चातप प्रसारयेत्।
  • नातभदेशे समुत्थाय नौकासनतमतत स्मतृ म्॥

questions.question: आसने शशाासनस्य प्राधां िववृण्वत ।
questions.solution_html:
• Sasankasana (also known as Shashankasana or Rabbit Pose) is a calming yoga
  • posture that involves bending forward from a kneeling position. It gently stretches
  • the spine, relieves tension in the back and shoulders, and promotes mental
  • relaxation by mimicking the resting posture of a hare.
  • वज्रासनतस्थतो योगी शशाङ्कासनमाचरेत।्
  • भुजौ प्रासाययपुरतः तशरः भूमौ तनवेशयेत्॥

questions.question: लोकायतदशनं िवशदयत |Explain about Lokayata philosophy.
questions.solution_html:
• Lokayata (also known as Charvaka) is an ancient, heterodox school of Indian
  • philosophy that emerged around 600 BCE, famous for its strictly materialist
  • empirical, and atheistic worldview. The term literally translates to "philosophy of
  • the people" or "worldly ones".

questions.question: प्राणायामस्य गुणाः के ?What are the benefits of Prāṇāyāma?
questions.solution_html:
• Pranayama: Rhythmic control of breath. Pranayama is the yogic art of breath
  • control. It improves physical and emotional health. It lowers stress, boosts lung
  • capacity, and helps you sleep better. Regular practice connects the mind and body.
questions.final_answer: capacity, and helps you sleep better. Regular practice connects the mind and body

questions.question: ानं िववृण्वत ।
questions.solution_html:
• Dhyana: Meditation or uninterrupted contemplation.
  • तत्र प्रत्ययैकतानता ध्यानम्

questions.question: हठयोगस्य प्रधानपुस्तकान् कािन?िवशदयत|Important text of Hathayoga.
questions.solution_html:
• Hatha Yoga is a system of physical and mental exercises designed to prepare
  • the body for deep meditation and spiritual awakening. Rooted in medieval India
  • the tradition emphasizes using the body as a vehicle to control the mind and
  • achieve enlightenment.Three major text are Hatha Yoga Pradipika (15th
  • Century)Author: Swami Swatmarama, Gheranda Samhita (17th Century)Author
  • Sage Gheranda and Shiva Samhita (15th to 18th Century).
questions.final_answer: Sage Gheranda and Shiva Samhita (15th to 18th Century)

questions.question: समग्रयोगायाःप्रयोजनािन कािन ?िवशदयत |Explain the purposes of holistic yoga.
questions.solution_html:
• The purpose of holistic yoga is to unite the mind, body, and spirit to create
  • deep harmony. Unlike simple exercise, it treats the whole person to build health
  • calm the mind, and reduce stress. It helps you live a balanced, peaceful life.
  • Holistic yoga achieves this through three main parts:Poses (Asanas): Physical
  • stretches that build strength and flexibility.Breathwork (Pranayama): Deep
  • breathing that calms the body and boosts energy.Meditation (Dhyana): Quiet focus
  • that clears the mind and promotes emotional peace.
questions.final_answer: that clears the mind and promotes emotional peace

questions.question: सांख्यदशनमिधकृ त्य िलखत |Write about Samkhya philosophy.
questions.solution_html:
• Samkhya (Sāṅkhya) is one of the oldest orthodox schools of Hindu
  • philosophy, traditionally founded by the sage Kapila. It is a system of metaphysical
  • dualism that explains the universe through an enumerative method, classifying
  • reality into 25 fundamental principles (tattvas).Samkhya divides all of reality into
  • two independent, eternal, and ultimate realities:Purusha : The pure
  • unchanging, eternal witness or spirit. It is devoid of qualities, does not act, and is
  • not a material object. In Samkhya, there are an infinite number of individual
  • Purushas.Prakriti (Nature/Matter): The primal, unconscious, yet active and creative
  • energy from which the entire physical and psychological universe evolves.
questions.final_answer: energy from which the entire physical and psychological universe evolves
